validity.researcher_notes: Length, diameter, capacity and status agree with the Gazprom pages. The 2014 trade journal gives a design capacity of 36 billion cubic meters a year and 650 km, which differ from the sheet only as design figures and rounding. The cost has no readable reference.

fills.researcher_notes: The Gazprom Proektirovanie encyclopedia page, read through the September 2024 archived copy, says the route of the Pochinki to Gryazovets pipeline is 653.2 km long. The sheet value of 653.2 is the same. The Gazprom project page gives 645 km and a 2014 trade journal gives 650 km, so other pages round the figure.

The same encyclopedia page gives a nominal diameter of 1400 mm and a working pressure of 7.4 MPa. The sheet value of 1400 is the same. The Gazprom project page and the 2014 trade journal both say 1420 mm. The 1400 and 1420 figures are the nominal and the outer designation of the same pipe, so the sheet value stays.

The Gazprom project page, read through the May 2025 archived copy, says the pipeline carries about 22 billion cubic meters of gas a year. The sheet value of 22 is the same. A 2014 trade journal gives a design capacity of up to 36 billion cubic meters a year. The two are different measures, a current figure and a design figure, so the operator's current figure stays.

The cost of 60 billion rubles is not in any page that could be read. The RBC page of December 2009 about the first 144 km was run through scripts/fetch.py (curl, TLS impersonation and the Chrome route), and all three failed on the site bot wall. It has no archived copy either. The Interfax page of September 2010 only lists the pipeline among the Gazprom investment priorities and gives no cost for it. The 2014 trade journal and the Gazprom pages give no cost. The sheet value stays and still needs a ref.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The Gazprom project page lists the pipeline as in service, and the 2014 trade journal says it was built from 2007 to 2012 and carries gas to the Northwest region.

cross_row_leads.note: The cost of 60 billion rubles may be in the RBC page of December 2009, which is blocked. A later search could look for a Gazprom report or a news item that gives the total cost.
